supplies.sleep: 1.6 uA (no RTC), 1.85 uA with RC RTC; power-down 0.8 uA (ds p14)
supplies.standby: STBY_RC 1.25 mA, STBY_XOSC 1.1 mA DC-DC (ds p14)
supplies.rx: 5.4-8.3 mA with DC-DC (sub-GHz LoRa 125 kHz 5.7 mA, boosted 7.8 mA; 2.4 GHz 6-8.3 mA) (ds p14)
supplies.tx: sub-GHz HP +22 dBm 118 mA @868/915, 100 mA @434/490; LP +14/15 dBm 28/36 mA; 2.4 GHz +13 dBm 26 mA; S-band +13 dBm 28 mA (ds p15)
supplies.tcxo: add TCXO current (1.5 mA nominal, regulator max 4 mA); VBAT must be >= VTCXO + 200 mV, so on a 3.3 V rail the highest usable setting is 3.0 V (RegTcxoTune 0x06) (UM p45, p47; ds p22)
supplies.regulator: LDO by default; SetRegMode(1) enables DC-DC in STBY_XOSC/FS/RX/TX (UM p41). +22 dBm needs VR_PA ~3.1 V, i.e. VBAT >= 3.3 V (UM p89)

logic.levels: VIH 0.7*VBAT, VIL 0.3*VBAT, VOH 0.9*VBAT, VOL 0.1*VBAT at 2.5 mA (ds p23). I/O level follows VBAT: 1.8 V I/O only if the whole chip runs at 1.8 V (then no +22 dBm). With VBAT = 3.3 V a 1.8 V pad cannot drive it (VIH 2.31 V).
logic.spi: mode 0 (CPOL=0, CPHA=0), up to 16 MHz, NSS falling to first SCK >= 31.25 ns, MISO high-Z when NSS high (ds p23)
logic.reset: NRESET low > 100 us (ds p25). Boot with a TCXO fitted: POR calibrations are skipped; host must SetTcxoMode then re-run calibration (ds p8)
logic.wake: from sleep: NSS low >= 100 us, NSS high, wait BUSY low (ds p24). NSS falling edge is the wake source, so the chip select must idle high and must not glitch
logic.busy: DIO0 high = cannot accept a command; host must wait for BUSY low before every SPI transaction (ds p9, p24)
logic.rfsw_defaults: all RFSW outputs high-Z until SetDioAsRfSwitch (ds p25, UM p38)

to_brain: SPI SCK/MOSI/MISO (shared radio SPI LPSPI6, 3.3 V)
BUSY (DIO0): should be a direct brain GPIO - it is polled before every command; NOT in the pin plan
IRQ (DIO9): direct brain GPIO preferred (packet timing); NOT in the pin plan
to_expander: NRESET (>100 us low pulse; fine on an expander)
IRQ (DIO9) may sit on an expander input with interrupt if a few ms of latency is acceptable
BUSY on an expander is workable only with slow command rates (an I2C read per SPI command)
RF switch controls need no host pins: DIO5/6/7/8/10 drive them

antenna.type: two 50 ohm ports: sub-GHz (after switch + match) and 1.9-2.5 GHz (RFIO_HF, already 50 ohm, needs harmonic filter). Semtech's figure shows a separate 'LoRa ANT' and 'S-band/2.4 GHz ANT' (ds p27 fig 4-1)
antenna.sharing: Sharing one connector with other transceivers is not described by Semtech. OpenRX-Mono (third-party) does put sub-GHz TX, sub-GHz RX and the 2.4 GHz path on one SP3T and one U.FL. Limits for a shared switch: max input 0 dBm on the sub-GHz path in operation, absolute max +10 dBm (ds p12)

notes: Semtech's own reference design packages (LR1121DVK1TxKS/TGKS design-file ZIPs, LR1121MB2THDAS, AN1200.59, AN1200.76) sit behind a Salesforce viewer that needs a browser session: NOT downloaded. Component values above therefore come from two third-party boards and from the datasheet/user manual text.
The datasheet's own schematic (p27 fig 4-1) is a block-level drawing without values.

For 150-960 MHz 'hack' coverage no single match exists; Semtech only describes 868/915 and 434/490 populations (UM p95 'multi-band operation' gives PA settings for one matching network, not component values).
OpenRX-Mono is CERN-OHL-S-2.0 (strongly reciprocal): copying its schematic would bind this board to that licence; here it is used only to cross-check values and JLCPCB codes.

KiCad: Connector_Coaxial:U.FL_Hirose_U.FL-R-SMT-1_Vertical, Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-363_SC-70-6 (PE4259), Crystal:Crystal_SMD_2016-4Pin_2.0x1.6mm, Crystal:Crystal_SMD_2012-2Pin_2.0x1.2mm exist. No standard footprint found for a 2016 TCXO (check the crystal 2016 pattern against the TCXO drawing) nor for SKY13373 QFN-12 2x2 P0.5 (LQFN-12-1EP_2x2mm_P0.5mm_EP0.7x0.7mm exists; check).
pin_plan_conflicts: BUSY, IRQ (DIO9) and NRESET have no pad or expander line in docs/hack-pad-pins.md; the plan's only free pad is STBY_REQ. At least BUSY wants a brain pad.
The chip select is a plain GPIO (DISP_B2_12): fine, but firmware must hold it low 100 us to wake the chip.

A 3.3 V TCXO cannot be powered from VTCXO on a 3.3 V rail (needs VBAT >= VTCXO + 0.2 V): use a part specified at <= 3.0 V, or feed the TCXO from +3V3 directly as OpenRX does (then it never switches off: about 1.5-2 mA in sleep unless its rail is switched).
